75663-porridge-poetry.title: Porridge Poetry
75663-porridge-poetry.creator: Unknown
75663-porridge-poetry.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. E POET] VERA VIRGINIA Oh, what a popular person I am! My full name is Vera Virginia Ham. The barn-dance, the two-step, the sausage-roll trot, The pig-jig, the hog-jog, I dance the whole lot. [Illustration: VERA VIRGINIA] THE LOLLIPOPINJAY On lollipops I live. I’m gay; I leap and swirl, I spin and sway. Come join me in the dance, I pray! Let’s go!--Slap-bang!--Hip, hip, hooray! For I’m the lollipopinjay. I loll by night, I dance all day.

arxiv-2102-11142.title: Minimum supports of eigenfunctions of graphs: a survey Note: The study was carried out within the framework of the state contract of the Sobolev Institute of Mathematics (project no. 0314-2019-0016). Journal: ADAM
arxiv-2102-11142.creator: Ev Sotnikova, Alexandr Valyuzhenich
arxiv-2102-11142.description: Abstract In this work we present a survey of results on the problem of finding the minimum cardinality of the support of eigenfunctions of graphs. 2010 MSC 05C50, 05E30, 05B30, 15A18 1 Introduction The eigenvalues of a graph are closely related to its structural properties and invariants (see the monographs [ 23 , 30 , 32 ] ).

arxiv-2108-00847.title: Large Deviations of Semi-supervised Learning in the Stochastic Block Model
arxiv-2108-00847.creator: Hugo Cui, Luca Saglietti, Lenka Zdeborová
arxiv-2108-00847.description: Abstract In community detection on graphs, the semi-supervised learning problem entails inferring the ground-truth membership of each node in a graph, given the connectivity structure and a limited number of revealed node labels. Different subsets of revealed labels can in principle lead to higher or lower information gains and induce different reconstruction accuracies.

arxiv-2108-06575.title: Refractive Geometry for Underwater Domes Journal: ArXiv submission
arxiv-2108-06575.creator: Mengkun She, David Nakath, Yifan Song, Kevin Köser
arxiv-2108-06575.description: Abstract Underwater cameras are typically placed behind glass windows to protect them from the water. Spherical glass, a dome port, is well suited for high water pressures at great depth, allows for a large field of view, and avoids refraction if a pinhole camera is positioned exactly at the sphere’s center.

arxiv-2411-03221.title: Perfect kernel of generalized Baumslag-Solitar groups
arxiv-2411-03221.creator: Sasha Bontemps
arxiv-2411-03221.description: Abstract Acknowledgements I am deeply grateful to my PhD advisor Damien Gaboriau for encouraging me to work on this subject and for the enlightening discussions that gave rise to the writing of this article. I also want to express my gratitude to François Le Maître and Yves Stalder for their useful remarks on the preliminary versions of this work.

arxiv-2511-19638.title: Concept drift of simple forecast models as a diagnostic of low-frequency, regime-dependent atmospheric reorganisation
arxiv-2511-19638.creator: Haokun Zhou
arxiv-2511-19638.description: Abstract Data-driven weather prediction models implicitly assume that the statistical relationship between predictors and targets is stationary. Under anthropogenic climate change, this assumption is violated, yet the structure of the resulting concept drift remains poorly understood. Here we introduce concept drift of simple forecast models as a diagnostic of atmospheric reorganisation.

arxiv-2512-09092.title: Explaining the Unseen: Multimodal Vision-Language Reasoning for Situational Awareness in Underground Mining Disasters
arxiv-2512-09092.creator: Mizanur Rahman Jewel, Mohamed Elmahallawy, Sanjay Madria, Samuel Frimpong
arxiv-2512-09092.description: Abstract Underground mining disasters produce pervasive darkness, dust, and collapses that obscure vision and make situational awareness difficult for humans and conventional systems. To address this, we propose MDSE , Multimodal Disaster Situation Explainer, a novel vision-language framework that automatically generates detailed textual explanations of post-disaster underground scenes.

europmc-pmc8417352.title: Global, regional, and national estimates and trends in stillbirths from 2000 to 2019: a systematic assessment.
europmc-pmc8417352.creator: Hug L, You D, Blencowe H, Mishra A, Wang Z, Fix MJ, Wakefield J, Moran AC, Gaigbe-Togbe V, Suzuki E, Blau DM, Cousens S, Creanga A, Croft T, Hill K, Joseph KS, Maswime S, McClure EM, Pattinson R, Pedersen J, Smith LK, Zeitlin J, Alkema L, UN Inter-agency Group for Child Mortality Estimation and its Core Stillbirth Estimation Group.

The UN Global Strategy for Women's, Children's and Adolescents' Health (2016-30) and the Every Newborn Action Plan (led by UNICEF and WHO) call for an

pmc-10597993.title: The prevalence and predictive factors of nocturnal polyuria in Japanese patients with nocturia: a multicentral retrospective cohort study
pmc-10597993.creator: Koji Iinuma, Yoshinori Nishino, Kanako Matsuoka, Tatsuya Ihara, Shunta Makabe, Ryo Tanji, Yuki Harigane, Kenichiro Ishida, Masayoshi Tamaki, Shigeaki Yokoi, Hiroki Hoshino, Kazuya Yuhara, Toru Yamada, Yasuaki Kubota, Kousei Miwa, Mina Kikuchi, Yoshiyuki Kojima, Takahiko Mitsui, Takuya Koie
pmc-10597993.description: The aims of this study were to determine the prevalence and predictors of nocturnal polyuria (NP) in Japanese patients. This multicentral, observational study enrolled patients with the chief complaint of nocturia at 17 Japanese institutions between January 2018 and December 2022. The frequency of daily voiding and volume of urination were evaluated using bladder diaries.

pmc-10617875.title: Cardiac papillary fibroelastoma: a rare cause of ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction: a case report
pmc-10617875.creator: Fnu Raheela, Abdul S Talpur, Michaela Rasmussen, Muhammad Jawad Farooq, Saad Khalid, Sadaf Bhat, Syed M Gilani, Sunita Shrestha
pmc-10617875.description: Introduction and importance:Primary tumors of the heart are extremely rare occurrences. Among them, cardiac papillary fibroelastoma (CPF) is the second most common type. Although these tumors are usually benign, they can pose a risk of embolization, which may lead to severe complications like sudden death or embolization affecting the neurological, systemic, or coronary vasculature. Such complications can be life-threatening.

pmc-10627869.title: Needle Arthroscopic Subchondroplasty With Adipose-Derived Stem Cell Augmentation for the Treatment of Osteochondral Lesions of the Talus
pmc-10627869.creator: Jari Dahmen, Cristian Indino, Riccardo D’Ambrosi, Federico G. Usuelli
pmc-10627869.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Needle arthroscopy has enjoyed a tremendous growth concerning the quality of intraoperative images due to technical innovation, resulting in innovative possibilities concerning concomitant minimally invasive procedures and treatment of osteochondral lesions of the talus (OLT). These lesions have increasingly been receiving scientific attention in the orthopaedic (sports) medicine field, and, as such, the quality of evidence-based treatment for them has developed substantially. Treatment of OLTs—and specifically subchondroplasty. OLTs may also be suitable for needle arthroscopic interventions.

pmc-10630340.title: UPrimer: A Clade-Specific Primer Design Program Based on Nested-PCR Strategy and Its Applications in Amplicon Capture Phylogenomics
pmc-10630340.creator: JiaXuan Li, GuangCheng Han, Xiao Tian, Dan Liang, Peng Zhang, Andrey Rzhetsky
pmc-10630340.description: Amplicon capture is a promising target sequence capture approach for phylogenomic analyses, and the design of clade-specific nuclear protein-coding locus (NPCL) amplification primers is crucial for its successful application. In this study, we developed a primer design program called UPrimer that can quickly design clade-specific NPCL amplification primers based on genome data, without requiring manual intervention.

pmc-10656429.title: Using Clinical Vignettes to Understand the Complexity of Diagnosing Type 1 Diabetes in Sub-Saharan Africa
pmc-10656429.creator: Enora Le Bec, Madibele Kam, Sigiriya Aebischer Perone, Philippa Boulle, Justin Cirhuza Cikomola, Maria Eugenia Gandur, Mario Gehri, Sylvia Kehlenbrink, David Beran
pmc-10656429.description: Lack of awareness, access to insulin and diabetes care can result in high levels of morbidity and mortality for children with type 1 diabetes (T1DM) in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA). Improvements in access to insulin and diabetes management have improved outcomes in some settings.

pmc-11367148.title: Neutral Red Labeling: A Novel Vital Staining Method for Investigating Central and Peripheral Nervous System Lesions
pmc-11367148.creator: Reiji Yamazaki, Nobuhiko Ohno
pmc-11367148.description: Multiple sclerosis, neuromyelitis optica, Guillain–Barré syndrome and chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy are representative demyelinating diseases of the central and peripheral nervous system. Remyelination by myelin forming cells is important for functional recovery from the neurological deficits caused in the demyelinating diseases. Lysophosphatidylcholine-induced demyelination in mice is commonly used to identify and study the molecular pathways of demyelination and remyelination.

pmc-11396210.title: Navigating the Neuroimmunomodulation Frontier: Pioneering Approaches and Promising Horizons—A Comprehensive Review
pmc-11396210.creator: Antea Krsek, Leona Ostojic, Dorotea Zivalj, Lara Baticic
pmc-11396210.description: The research in neuroimmunomodulation aims to shed light on the complex relationships that exist between the immune and neurological systems and how they affect the human body. This multidisciplinary field focuses on the way immune responses are influenced by brain activity and how neural function is impacted by immunological signaling. This provides important insights into a range of medical disorders.

pmc-11587489.title: Assessing the Impact of a Leadership Development Programme for Community Pharmacy Neighbourhood Leads in South East London
pmc-11587489.creator: Finlay Royle, Sarah Guard, Ricarda Micallef, Jon Schommer
pmc-11587489.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Community pharmacists continue to deliver a growing number of services, with an increased need for collaborative work between local teams in community settings. In South East London, the Integrated Care Board and Pharmacy Alliance have invested in the development of community pharmacy neighbourhood leads (CPNLs), who represent community pharmacies in a locality and provided a tailored five-session leadership course that ran between November 2023 and March 2024, covering theory and implementation.

pmc-11716618.title: Estimating preclinical amyloid positivity in the community: a case study transporting estimates from ADNI to ARIC
pmc-11716618.creator: Emma K Stapp, Elizabeth Rose Mayeda, Elizabeth A Stuart, Rebecca F. Gottesman, Dean F. Wong, Thomas H. Mosley, Michael E. Griswold, M. Maria Glymour, Scott C Zimmerman, Melinda C Power
pmc-11716618.description: BackgroundEstimates of the prevalence of preclinical amyloid positivity in the US general population are of great interest to the field, but difficult to measure and thus unavailable in representative studies. A statistical approach from causal inference, ‘transport’, may allow for improved generalizability of findings from a sample of persons from one population to another.

pmc-12467520.title: DAGMNet: Dual-Branch Attention-Pruned Graph Neural Network for Multimodal sMRI and fMRI Fusion in Autism Prediction
pmc-12467520.creator: Lanlan Wang, Xinyu Li, Jialu Yuan, Yinghao Chen, Catarina Morais Seabra
pmc-12467520.description: Background: Accurate and early diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is essential for timely intervention. Structural magnetic resonance imaging (sMRI) and functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) provide complementary insights into brain structure and function. Most deep learning approaches rely on a single modality, limiting their ability to capture cross-modal relationships.

pmc-12646343.title: A Bibliometric Analysis of Drug Resistance in Pediatric Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia
pmc-12646343.creator: Alireza Khanahmad, Mohammad Hossein Khazaee-Nasirabadi, Mahshid Lotfi, Amir Hami
pmc-12646343.description: Background:Despite the improved outcomes in acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL), drug resistance remains a major challenge. This study provides the first overview of global research trends in pediatric ALL drug resistance, highlighting emerging directions.Materials and Methods:In this bibliometric study, related keywords such as acute lymphoblastic leukemia, pediatric, and drug resistance were searched in the Web of Science (WOS) Core Collection.

pmc-12698595.title: Respiratory microbiome-host interaction on lung carcinogenesis, immunity, and immunotherapy
pmc-12698595.creator: Peng Wang, Cuihong Ge, Xinru Jing, Qijia Han, Mingzhu Wang, Minghua Huang, Zhiming Xiang
pmc-12698595.description: The respiratory microbiome, as an integral component of the lung cancer microenvironment, exerts pivotal influences on tumorigenesis, immune homeostasis, and therapeutic response through intricate crosstalk with host immunity. Despite advancements, current limitations in lung cancer immunotherapy persist, including heterogeneous therapeutic responses, immune-related adverse events, and the lack of predictive biomarkers.

pmc-12870924.title: Association of endocrine autoantibodies (anti-TPO, anti-GAD, anti-insulin) with histopathological severity in pediatric Celiac disease: a retrospective cohort study
pmc-12870924.creator: Büşra Tetik Dinçer, Nafiye Urgancı, Aybike Koç, Hatice Kup, Merve Usta
pmc-12870924.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). PurposeCeliac disease (CD) is an autoimmune disorder triggered by gluten ingestion, characterized by the development of specific autoantibodies. An increased incidence of type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) and autoimmune thyroid disease (ATD) has been reported in patients with CD. However, there is a gap in the literature regarding the association between the severity of CD and the levels of these autoantibodies.

pmc-13080210.title: Editorial: Clinical and surgical perspectives in sublobar resection for lung cancer
pmc-13080210.creator: Takuya Fujita
pmc-13080210.description: c standards. In this Research Topic, we feature a series of articles on the latest advancements in Sublobar Resection for Lung Cancer. We hope that these insights will provide valuable, actionable knowledge for your clinical practice. Five highly excellent papers were published Magouliotis et al.

pmc-13203635.title: Effects of Soil Substrates and Microbial Inoculants on Earthworm-Mediated Modification of Soil Structure and Physicochemical Properties
pmc-13203635.creator: Hong Zhu, Xiaowei Cui, Wenyi Sheng, Yuzhi Wang, Xiao Wang, Pengcheng Zhu, Ning Du, Zhaojie Cui, Hongnian Chen, Jierui Dai, Lele Liu, Weihua Guo
pmc-13203635.description: Simple SummaryHealthy soil is needed to grow food and support nature, but many soils have become degraded. In this study, we tested whether adding different materials such as compost (organic fertilizer), a mining byproduct called coal gangue, and beneficial bacteria could help earthworms improve soil quality. We tested these materials alone and together in a controlled experiment.

pmc-13220661.title: Solvation of CaCl2 at the Water–Vapor Interface Revealed by Ambient Pressure X‑ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy
pmc-13220661.creator: Andreas Siebert, Kritanjan Polley, Shane W. Devlin, Mauricio Lopez Luna, N. Isaac Zakaria, Nykita Rustad, David T. Limmer, Monika Blum
pmc-13220661.description: The determination of ion concentrations at aqueous interfaces is of paramount importance for the precise modeling of atmospheric reactions. Despite their significant concentrations observed in bulk sea spray aerosol studies, the concentration of Ca2+ ions at the liquid–vapor interface remains unclear.

pmc-13361434.title: Therapeutic Exercise for Forward Head Posture in Neck Pain Patients: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
pmc-13361434.creator: Yachen Xing, Ronghui Wang, Xingrui Zhao, Anjie Xu
pmc-13361434.description: BackgroundForward Head Posture (FHP) is a prevalent musculoskeletal disorder strongly associated with neck pain and functional disability. Although therapeutic exercise is commonly recommended in clinical practice, there remains a lack of consensus regarding the most effective exercise modalities and optimal intervention duration.

pmc-13457188.title: Potential plastic biodegradation in lakes worldwide
pmc-13457188.creator: Qi Zhang, Zhenyan Zhang, Ziyao Zhang, Guoyan Qin, Mingkang Jin, Bingfeng Chen, Yitian Yu, Tingzhang Wang, Meixia Wang, Tao Lu, Dong Zhu, Li Cui, Haifeng Qian, Matthias C. Rillig, Yong-Guan Zhu
pmc-13457188.description: Plastic pollution is ubiquitous, yet the biodegradation of plastic waste remains poorly understood due to limited knowledge of microbial plastic degradation potential. Here, we demonstrate that plastic waste shapes the global distribution of plastic-degrading potential across 182,661 lakes worldwide using integrated metagenomic and machine learning analyses and identify a tipping point (≥7.44 particles/m3) for effective in situ bioremediation.

pmc-13568291.title: Sustained Remission Following Limited Dupilumab Exposure in Refractory Eosinophilic Esophagitis
pmc-13568291.creator: Dain (Raina) Kim, Adam Bubelenyi, Milli Gupta
pmc-13568291.description: Eosinophilic esophagitis (EoE) is a type 2 immune-mediated esophageal disorder that can be refractory to standard therapy. We present a case of a 49-year-old woman with asthma, chronic sinusitis, and nasal polyposis diagnosed with EoE refractory to proton pump inhibitors, dietary modification, and swallowed topical corticosteroids.
